records.issue_text: limit and offset in GroupsController#members are parsed via .to_i with no clamping; negative values cause a PostgreSQL OFFSET error (500) and large limits allow dumping entire automatic groups in one request
records.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` in GroupsController#members with no clamping before `members.limit(limit).offset(offset)`. A negative offset produces invalid SQL in PostgreSQL (500), and an unbounded limit allows dumping the entire group membership in one request. Only the frontend clamps offset; the endpoint accepts arbitrary params.

records.issue_text: Missing tests for adding an existing member, removing a non-member/nonexistent user id, update changing alias_level, and pagination meta in GroupsController#members
records.rationale: The finding is accurate and specific: the diff adds new endpoints and behavior with only happy-path tests. add_members tests only a fresh two-user add (no duplicate/existing-member case); remove_member tests only a valid member removal; .update tests only name/visible changes — no test covers alias_level updating (params[:alias_level].to_i logic in update); GroupsController#members pagination meta (limit/offset/total) has no spec coverage despite being newly added nontrivial logic. This is grounded in the diff's new controller code and spec file, and is a substantive non-bug review concern abo

records.issue_text: No error handling (popupAjaxError) on addMembers/removeMember PUT/DELETE in group.js model and controller, so 422/500 failures are silent and the usernames input is never cleared
records.rationale: The diff's new addMembers/removeMember in group.js end with .then(...reload...) and no .catch/popupAjaxError, and the controller actions (addMembers, removeMember) also lack error handling, so a 422/500 (e.g., automatic group rejection rendered by can_not_modify_automatic) is swallowed silently. The claim is verifiable in the diff: no error path exists for these new ajax calls. Severity is UX-level, but it is a genuine defect in newly added code.
